## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Sūkaramukhapetavatthu* (Pv 2) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. Translated into English as *The Story of a Ghost With a Pig’s Mouth*, its central moral lesson is that even the use of harsh speech is enough to cause severe karmic retribution and suffering in the afterlife.

 Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies five Pali-internal matches between Pv 2 and its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with the longest shared passage occurring across segments 3.1–3.4 (aligned with commentary segments 68–69); no cross-language matches above threshold are detected [DharmaNexus].
